narrative: The model estimates your chance of failing the final year at about 35%, so this is a risk flag rather than a certainty: roughly one in three students with a similar profile would fail, and because you fall into the predicted-fail group, remedial courses are being required. The strongest influence on this judgment was your reason for choosing the school: coming because of its reputation pushed the prediction toward passing. The second most important factor was your one past class failure, compared with an average of none among students who passed; this pushed toward failing. The third was your low amount of free time, which also pushed slightly toward passing. In other words, two of the three leading factors worked in your favor, but they were not enough to offset the overall risk pattern, which is why the model still estimates a 35% failure chance and requires remedial support. Your profile also shows less than two hours of weekly study, while most passing students study two to five hours; you have internet access and want higher education, which are strengths. To improve, treat the past failure as a warning, build a regular study routine above two hours, use available family support, and ask your teachers for a focused plan to close gaps. Remedial courses are the next step to reduce the risk.
